title: Clearing a Counter Register
statement: Let $M$ be a multitape Turing machine with Boolean tape symbols, let $x$ be a finite Boolean input, let $s$ be one of the three clearing modes, let $\rho$ assign a natural-number value to each of eleven registers, and let $p$ be a natural-number input position. For every output word $o$, the counter program started at phase $0$ of the clearing routine for $s$, with registers $\rho$, input position $p$, and output $o$, reaches the exit for $s$ in at most $2\rho(r)+1$ steps, where $r$ is the register selected by $s$; at that point only $r$ has changed, its value is $0$, the input position is still $p$, and the output is still $o$.
